summary: Ported the complete three-phase RVV proposal from the related open work onto the prepared main checkout: RVV 1.0 C++ kernels and unit tests, Python dispatch and attention-backend integration, and the RISC-V Docker/documentation path. Adapted CPU backend selection to the current arg_groups resolution architecture and added compatibility/adversarial regression coverage. The prepared host is x86_64 and has no RVV device or RISC-V sysroot/toolchain, so this is an unqualified candidate rather than a claim that the feature is fully verified.

tests.what_was_measured: RVV suite collection and non-hardware integration/fallback behavior on x86_64: 14 passed and 49 hardware kernel tests skipped. No RVV numerical execution occurred.

Current server-argument compatibility, RVV default selection, preservation of an explicit backend, backend registration, metadata guards, cache wiring, fallback semantics, and weight-packing behavior: 21 passed.

tests.command: PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-d2960c95291c/pre-commit SKIP=no-commit-to-branch /opt/venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed Python and RVV C++ files>
tests.what_was_measured: Repository formatting and static hooks for the changed Python and C++ implementation: isort, Ruff lint/format, codespell, clang-format, AST and conflict checks all passed on the final rerun.

Attempted independent RVV compiler validation. The pinned ROCm Clang 22 installation lacks riscv_vector.h, so it cannot compile RVV intrinsics; raw diagnostic is retained in rvv-vector-math-clang.log.

remaining_limitations: No RISC-V/RVV 1.0 hardware was assigned; all 49 native kernel numerical tests were skipped on the x86_64 host.
No GPU was used: the requested backend targets RISC-V CPUs, and an unrelated GPU smoke would not validate RVV execution.

The available pinned Clang 22 is ROCm-specific and does not ship riscv_vector.h; no RISC-V sysroot or Clang 19+ RVV toolchain was available, so the native library was not rebuilt or inspected for emitted RVV instructions.

Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GSM8K accuracy and RVV-versus-Torch-native performance were not run because they require a supported RISC-V board and model weights. The tiny Llama serving fixture cannot qualify this architecture, RVV numerical accuracy, or performance, so it was not substituted.
The Docker image was not built because the current node is x86_64 and the documented image requires native linux/riscv64 dependencies, including vendor-provided wheels.
The linked upstream Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3 changes remain open and their published hardware results were inspected but not independently reproduced here.
